name: Mazdutide
status_note: Approved only in China, for chronic weight management (June 2025) and type 2 diabetes (September 2025); investigational elsewhere, where Eli Lilly holds the rights.
evidence_note: Approved on the basis of phase 3 trials in Chinese adults (GLORY-1, GLORY-2, DREAMS-1, DREAMS-2 and DREAMS-3; about 2,500 participants in total) plus phase 1–2 trials in China and the US; there are no cardiovascular-outcome or phase 3 data outside China yet.
tagline: Once-weekly glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist approved in China for obesity and diabetes
summary: Mazdutide is a synthetic analogue of the gut hormone oxyntomodulin that activates both the GLP-1 receptor and the glucagon receptor, with a fatty-acid tail that allows once-weekly injection. Discovered by Eli Lilly and developed in China by Innovent Biologics, it became the first glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist approved anywhere when China authorised it as Xinermei for weight management in June 2025, followed by type 2 diabetes. In phase 3 trials it produced about 14% average weight loss at 6 mg over 48 weeks and about 17% at 9 mg over 60 weeks.
overview: Oxyntomodulin is a 37-amino-acid peptide released from intestinal L-cells alongside GLP-1. It consists of the complete glucagon sequence plus an eight-residue C-terminal extension (KRNRNNIA) and activates both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, and a small 2005 trial showed that injected oxyntomodulin reduced body weight in people with overweight and obesity. The native hormone is quickly inactivated by the enzyme DPP-4, so several companies set out to build long-acting 'oxyntomodulin analogues' that combine GLP-1-driven appetite suppression with the metabolic effects of glucagon.

Mazdutide is Eli Lilly's version, described in a patent application with a 2015 priority date. Serine 2 is replaced by the non-natural amino acid Aib to block DPP-4; glutamate, lysine and leucine substitutions at positions 16–28 raise potency and stability (Met27→Leu prevents oxidation, Asn28→Glu avoids deamidation and improves solubility); the basic KRNRNNIA tail is replaced by the short sequence GPSSG; and lysine 20 carries a C20 fatty diacid on a γGlu-2×OEG linker that binds albumin. According to the patent, the length and position of the fatty acid were critical for keeping activity at the two receptors roughly balanced.

Lilly began human studies in 2016 and in 2019 licensed the Chinese rights to Innovent Biologics, which developed the compound under the code IBI362. Phase 3 trials in 610 Chinese adults with obesity or overweight (GLORY-1) and about 1,050 adults with type 2 diabetes (DREAMS-1 and DREAMS-2) led to approval by China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in June 2025 for chronic weight management and in September 2025 for type 2 diabetes. A head-to-head trial then showed better combined glucose and weight control than semaglutide 1 mg (DREAMS-3), and a higher 9 mg dose tested in GLORY-2 has been under review in China since November 2025.

Outside China the rights remain with Lilly, which has tested doses of up to 16 mg in US trials, including a phase 2 study in which the 16 mg dose produced 18.1% average weight loss at 32 weeks but led one in five participants to stop treatment because of side effects. Further trials are exploring fatty liver disease, obstructive sleep apnoea, heart failure, adolescent obesity and alcohol use disorder.
mechanism: Mazdutide is an agonist at two class B G-protein-coupled receptors, the GLP-1 receptor and the glucagon receptor. Through the GLP-1 receptor it acts like other incretin drugs: it increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon release from the pancreas, slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite through receptors in the brain.

Glucagon receptors are concentrated in the liver, where their activation promotes lipolysis and fatty-acid oxidation and inhibits fat synthesis; glucagon is also thought to raise energy expenditure. In preclinical studies mazdutide lowered body weight even in mice lacking either receptor and, unlike semaglutide, increased energy expenditure. The GLP-1 component counterbalances glucagon's tendency to raise blood glucose, and in trials HbA1c fell substantially while liver fat dropped by about 70–80% in participants with fatty liver at baseline.
origin: Synthetic analogue of oxyntomodulin, a 37-amino-acid proglucagon-derived hormone from intestinal L-cells that activates both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors

discovery.by: Adam R. Mezo, Yanyun Chen, Francisco A. Valenzuela, Hongchang Qu and colleagues, Eli Lilly
discovery.where: Eli Lilly and Company, United States
discovery.note: Lilly's patent on balanced glucagon/GLP-1 co-agonists (priority date 22 June 2015; US 9,938,335) describes the molecule as compound 2, the C20-diacid member of a series built on a modified oxyntomodulin backbone.

first_approval.indication: Chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight

developer: Eli Lilly and Company (originator); Innovent Biologics (development and commercialisation in China)

brands.name: Xinermei (信尔美)
brands.use: Chronic weight management; glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes

analogs.name: Oxyntomodulin
analogs.note: Native 37-residue proglucagon product (glucagon plus KRNRNNIA) on which mazdutide is based; short-acting

analogs.name: Survodutide (BI 456906)
analogs.note: Another fatty-acylated glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist, from Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand Pharma

modifications.label: Aib2 (α-aminoisobutyric acid) replaces Ser2 of oxyntomodulin and protects the N-terminus from cleavage by DPP-4
Lys20 carries an icosanedioic (C20) fatty diacid attached through γ-glutamate and two OEG (8-amino-3,6-dioxaoctanoic acid) spacers; it binds serum albumin
Leu27 replaces Met27 of oxyntomodulin to prevent methionine oxidation
Glu28 replaces Asn28 to avoid deamidation and improve solubility

sequence.note: 34 residues, per the FDA GSRS/INN definition, KEGG D12225 and Lilly's patent (compound 2). Positions 1–29 follow oxyntomodulin/glucagon numbering; residues 30–34 (GPSSG, ending in a glycinamide) replace the KRNRNNIA tail of oxyntomodulin. The linker runs Lys20 Nε–OEG–OEG–γGlu–C20 diacid.

half_life: Long; terminal half-life of about 6–17 days after a first dose in a phase 1b study, supporting once-weekly dosing

structure.notes: No experimental structure of mazdutide is in the PDB (searches for mazdutide, IBI362 and LY3305677 return no entries). PubChem's mazdutide record (CID 167312357) depicts a 33-residue peptide lacking one of the two serines before the C-terminal glycinamide (formula C207H317N45O65), so it is not linked here; the 34-residue structure (C210H322N46O67, calculated MW 4563.1) follows the FDA GSRS/INN definition, KEGG and Lilly's patent.

approved.detail: Adults with a BMI of at least 28 kg/m², or at least 24 kg/m² with one or more weight-related conditions (Chinese cut-offs), alongside diet and physical activity (GLORY-1).
Glycaemic control in adults, alone or with metformin, sulfonylureas or SGLT2 inhibitors (DREAMS-1 and DREAMS-2).

investigational.stage: Phase 3 — positive; under review in China
investigational.detail: GLORY-2: in 462 adults with a BMI of 30 or more, 9 mg weekly reduced body weight by 16.7% at 60 weeks versus 1.5% with placebo; a supplementary application was accepted in November 2025.
Lilly's US phase 2 trial in 179 adults found 15.6% (10 mg) and 18.1% (16 mg) weight loss at 32 weeks versus 0.9% with placebo; 20% stopped the 16 mg dose because of adverse events.

investigational.use: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease and MASH
investigational.detail: GLORY-3 compares mazdutide 9 mg with semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity and fatty liver disease; a separate phase 2 trial enrols people with MASH.
GLORY-OSA enrols Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe sleep apnoea and obesity (first participant dosed June 2025).
After a 12-week phase 1b trial in 36 adolescents aged 12–17 (BMI down 8.8% with 4 mg and 11.0% with 6 mg versus 1.7% with placebo), a registrational phase 3 trial began in December 2025.

investigational.use: Heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction
investigational.detail: Trial in Chinese adults with HFpEF or HFmrEF and obesity.

off_label.detail: Outside China, where no mazdutide product is approved, FDA reports that companies have illegally sold unapproved products said to contain mazdutide, falsely labelled 'for research purposes' but marketed with dosing instructions for people to inject.
off_label.evidence: Clinical data apply only to the genuine drug used under medical supervision; the identity, dose, purity and sterility of grey-market products are unknown.

history.title: Lilly patents balanced glucagon/GLP-1 co-agonists
history.detail: Lilly's patent application described oxyntomodulin analogues with Aib2, a lipidated Lys20 and a GPSSG C-terminus; mazdutide corresponds to its compound 2, carrying a C20 diacid.

history.title: First human dosing
history.detail: Lilly began a single-ascending-dose study of LY3305677 in healthy volunteers, followed by multiple-dose and type 2 diabetes studies.

history.title: Innovent licenses the Chinese rights
history.detail: Innovent Biologics announced an agreement with Lilly to develop and commercialise the oxyntomodulin analogue, then called OXM3, in China; Lilly retained the rights elsewhere.

history.title: First trial in China
history.detail: Innovent's phase 1b study of IBI362 began; in 36 adults with overweight or obesity, 12 weeks of treatment reduced body weight by up to 6.4% versus a 0.6% gain with placebo.

history.title: 9 mg dose gives 18.6% placebo-adjusted weight loss
history.detail: In an 80-person phase 2 cohort with a mean BMI of 34.3, mazdutide 9 mg produced a placebo-adjusted weight loss of 18.6% after 48 weeks.

history.title: GLORY-1 succeeds and an application is filed
history.detail: The first phase 3 obesity trial met all primary and key secondary endpoints; China's Center for Drug Evaluation accepted the new drug application for chronic weight management on 7 February 2024.

history.title: DREAMS-2 beats dulaglutide
history.detail: In type 2 diabetes both mazdutide doses were superior to dulaglutide 1.5 mg for HbA1c and weight reduction; a diabetes application was accepted in August 2024.

history.title: GLORY-1 published in the NEJM
history.detail: In 610 Chinese adults, weight fell by 11.0% (4 mg) and 14.0% (6 mg) at 48 weeks versus a 0.3% gain with placebo.

history.title: China approves Xinermei for weight management
history.detail: The NMPA approved mazdutide 4 mg and 6 mg for chronic weight management, making it the world's first approved glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist.

history.title: Type 2 diabetes approval
history.detail: The NMPA approved mazdutide for glycaemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, as monotherapy or with metformin, sulfonylureas or SGLT2 inhibitors.

history.title: DREAMS-3: better than semaglutide
history.detail: In 349 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity, 48.0% on mazdutide 6 mg reached an HbA1c below 7% with at least 10% weight loss at 32 weeks, versus 21.0% on semaglutide 1 mg.

history.title: GLORY-2 tests a 9 mg dose
history.detail: The 60-week phase 3 trial in adults with a BMI of 30 or more met all primary and key secondary endpoints; a supplementary application for the 9 mg dose was accepted for review on 25 November 2025.

history.title: Diabetes trials published in Nature
history.detail: DREAMS-1 (versus placebo) and DREAMS-2 (versus dulaglutide), together 1,051 participants, appeared back-to-back in Nature.

history.title: High-dose results published
history.detail: JAMA published GLORY-2 (16.7% versus 1.5% weight loss at 60 weeks), and Lilly's US phase 2 trial in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology reported 18.1% weight loss at 32 weeks with 16 mg.

regulatory.detail: Xinermei approved by the NMPA for chronic weight management (27 June 2025) and type 2 diabetes (September 2025) at 4 mg and 6 mg; a 9 mg dose for moderate-to-severe obesity has been under review since November 2025.
Not approved. Eli Lilly, which holds the rights outside China, has completed phase 1 and phase 2 trials in the US at doses of up to 16 mg.
Approved in China, so the S0 'non-approved substances' rule does not apply; GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonists are not on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list.

pk.half_life: Terminal half-life ranged from about 6 to 17 days (151–404 h) after a first dose in Chinese adults with obesity
pk.tmax: Median about 72 hours after subcutaneous injection

dosing.regimen: Once-weekly subcutaneous injection at maintenance doses of 4 mg or 6 mg. In the phase 3 trials that supported approval, treatment started at 2 mg weekly for 4 weeks and was raised in 4-week steps (2 → 4 mg, or 2 → 4 → 6 mg).

dosing_note: Approved only in China. The regimen is summarised from the approval announcements and the phase 3 trial protocols for reference; follow the local prescribing information and a clinician's advice.

serious: Gastrointestinal intolerance leading to discontinuation, more frequent at higher doses (0.5–1.5% at 4–6 mg in GLORY-1, 2.9% at 9 mg in GLORY-2, 20% at 16 mg in a US phase 2 trial)
safety.notes: Gastrointestinal effects were mostly mild to moderate and concentrated in the dose-escalation period. In GLORY-1, serious adverse events were infrequent and similar to placebo, and mean heart rate was about 1.6 beats per minute higher than baseline at 48 weeks. Long-term safety and cardiovascular-outcome data are not yet available.

facts: Mazdutide was the first glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist approved anywhere in the world (China, June 2025).

Its C-terminal Gly-Gly-Pro-Ser-Ser-Gly segment is identical to residues 29–34 of exendin-4; Lilly's patent reports that this short GPSSG tail gave better in vivo potency and stability than oxyntomodulin's own C-terminus.
In the head-to-head DREAMS-3 trial, 48% of people on mazdutide 6 mg reached both an HbA1c below 7% and at least 10% weight loss, versus 21% on semaglutide 1 mg.
Rights are split geographically: Innovent develops and sells mazdutide in China, while Eli Lilly keeps the rights in the rest of the world.
